verses.english: Linked Discourses 11.5
Chapter One
Victory by Good Speech
At Sāvatthī.
“Once upon a time, mendicants, a battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Vepacitti, lord of titans, said to Sakka, lord of gods,
‘Lord of gods, let there be victory by fine words!’
‘Vepacitti, let there be victory by fine words!’

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, devā ca asurā ca pārisajje ṭhapesuṁ:
verses.english: Then the gods and the titans appointed a panel of judges, saying,
‘These will understand our good and bad statements.’

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Vepacitti, lord of titans, said to Sakka, lord of gods,
‘Lord of gods, recite a verse!’

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vepacittiṁ asurindaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, Sakka said to him,
‘Vepacitti, you are the elder gods here.
Recite a verse.’

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
verses.english: So Vepacitti spoke this verse:
‘Fools would vent even more
if there’s no-one to put a stop to them.
So an intelligent person should stop
a fool with forceful punishment.’

verses.pali: Bhāsitāya kho pana, bhikkhave, vepacittinā asurindena gāthāya asurā anumodiṁsu, devā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
verses.english: The titans applauded Vepacitti’s verse, while the gods kept silent.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Vepacitti said to Sakka,
‘Lord of gods, recite a verse!’

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
verses.english: So Sakka spoke this verse:
‘I think that this is the only way
to put a stop to a fool,
when you know that the other is upset,
be mindful and stay calm.’

verses.pali: Bhāsitāya kho pana, bhikkhave, sakkena devānamindena gāthāya, devā anumodiṁsu, asurā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
verses.english: The gods applauded Sakka’s verse, while the titans kept silent.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vepacittiṁ asurindaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Sakka said to Vepacitti,
‘Vepacitti, recite a verse!’

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
verses.english: So Vepacitti spoke this verse:
‘In this mere endurance, Vāsava,
I see a flaw.
When a fool thinks,
“He endures me out of fear,”
the simpleton will go after you even harder,
like a cow chasing someone who runs away.’

verses.pali: Bhāsitāya kho pana, bhikkhave, vepacittinā asurindena gāthāya asurā anumodiṁsu, devā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
verses.english: The titans applauded Vepacitti’s verse, while the gods kept silent.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Vepacitti said to Sakka,
‘Lord of gods, recite a verse!’

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
verses.english: So Sakka spoke this verse:
‘Let him think this if he wishes, or not—
“He endures me out of fear.”
For the highest goal, one’s own,
naught better than patience is found.
When a strong person
endures a weakling,
they call that the ultimate patience,
for a weakling must always be patient.
The strength of folly
is really just weakness, they say.
But no-one can challenge a person
who’s strong, guarded by the teaching.
When you get angry at an angry person
you just make things worse for yourself.
When you don’t get angry at an angry person
you win a battle hard to win.
When you know that the other is angry,
you act for the good of both
yourself and the other
if you’re mindful and stay calm.
People inexpert in the teaching
consider one who heals both
oneself and the other
to be a fool.’

verses.pali: Bhāsitāsu kho pana, bhikkhave, sakkena devānamindena gāthāsu, devā anumodiṁsu, asurā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
verses.english: The gods applauded Sakka’s verses, while the titans kept silent.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, devānañca asurānañca pārisajjā etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: Then the panel of judges consisting of both gods and titans said this,
‘The verses spoken by Vepacitti

verses.pali: Tā ca kho sadaṇḍāvacarā sasatthāvacarā, iti bhaṇḍanaṁ iti viggaho iti kalaho.
verses.english: evoke punishment and violence. That’s how you get fights, arguments, and quarrels.
The verses spoken by Sakka

verses.pali: Tā ca kho adaṇḍāvacarā asatthāvacarā, iti abhaṇḍanaṁ iti aviggaho iti akalaho.
verses.english: don’t evoke punishment and violence. That’s how you stay free of fights, arguments, and quarrels.
Sakka, lord of gods, wins victory by fine words!’

verses.pali: Iti kho, bhikkhave, sakkassa devānamindassa subhāsitena jayo ahosī”ti.
verses.english: And that’s how Sakka came to win victory by fine words.”
